title: Smooth transition coefficient subrings of a characteristic-zero field
statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero [def-weil-field]. There exist a small nonempty directed partially ordered set $D$ and subrings $R_i\subseteq k$ containing $\mathbf Q$, for $i\in D$, with the following properties. Each $R_i$ is a finite type $\mathbf Q$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and is smooth over $\mathbf Q$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. If $i\leq j$ then $R_i\subseteq R_j$, and this inclusion is smooth. The union of these subrings is $k$, and the inclusions exhibit $k$ as their ring colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Each inclusion $R_i\to k$ is regular [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. No claim is made that every inclusion between arbitrary smooth $\mathbf Q$-subalgebras of $k$ is smooth.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman--Temkin, Theorem 7.5(1), proof for fields, with Definition 7.2 and Remark 7.3(1): take affine rational models of Spec(k), then their schematic images in k. Regularity of projections is Definition 7.2; regular finite-type transitions are smooth. Read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED. No specialized Stacks tag; underlying smooth-colimit regularity is Tag 07EP, more-algebra-lemma-colimit-smooth-regular.

proof.text: Identify $\mathbf Q$ with its prime subfield in $k$. By [lem-exc-transcendence-basis-exists], choose a transcendence basis $B\subseteq k$ over $\mathbf Q$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis]. Put $A_T=\mathbf Q[t\mid t\in T]\subseteq k$ and $F_T=\mathbf Q(T)=\operatorname{Frac}(A_T)$ for each finite $T\subseteq B$. Algebraic independence identifies $A_T$ with a polynomial ring. The extension $k/\mathbf Q(B)$ is algebraic and separable: an irreducible polynomial in characteristic zero has nonzero derivative of smaller degree, hence is relatively prime to its derivative. This also proves separability for every algebraic extension of any $F_T$ used below.

source.place: Tag 030F, lemma-transcendence-degree; elementary derivative argument following Tag 09H0, lemma-irreducible-polynomials.

proof.text: Given a finite subset $S\subseteq k$ and a prescribed finite $T_0\subseteq B$, [lem-weil-pbc-separating-transcendence-basis-finite-subextension] supplies a finite $T\subseteq B$ such that $F_T(S)/F_T$ is finite separable. Replace $T$ by $U=T\cup T_0$. The same finitely many elements of $S$ are algebraic over $F_U$: their polynomials over $F_T$ remain nonzero over $F_U$. Successively adjoining these elements gives a finite-dimensional extension $L=F_U(S)$ of $F_U$ (products of the bounded powers of the generators span it). Its separability follows from the characteristic-zero derivative argument in Step 1. Thus the finite-subextension conclusion can always be arranged with $U\supseteq T_0$.

source.place: Tag 030U, lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness, second proof paragraph, finite-subset observation; prescribed variables added explicitly.

proof.text:
The polynomial domain $A_U$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], since $\mathbf Q$ has only the ideals $0$ and $\mathbf Q$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spread-finite-separable-extension] to $A_U$, its fraction field $F_U$, and the finite separable extension $L$ of Step 2. Obtain $0
e c\in A_U$ and a domain $C$, finite etale over $A_U[1/c]$, with its specified fraction-field identification $\operatorname{Frac}(C)=L$. Use this identification to regard $C$ as a subring of $L\subseteq k$. Write each $s\in S$ as $a_s/b_s$ with $a_s,b_s\in C$ and $b_s
e0$, and put $b=\prod_{s\in S}b_s$ (the empty product is $1$). Then $R=C[1/b]\subseteq k$ contains $S$, since $a_s/b_s=a_s\prod_{s'
e s}b_{s'}/b$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization], $R$ is etale over $A_U[1/c]$. The identity of $A_U$ is etale: take the monic polynomial $Q(Z)=Z$ in [lem-weil-pbc-standard-etale-monic-derivative], whose algebra is $A_U[Z,Y]/(Z,Y-1)=A_U$. The localization clause of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization] applied to this identity makes $A_U	o A_U[1/c]$ etale. Composition [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] shows $\operatorname{Spec}R	o\operatorname{Spec}A_U$ is etale. We have proved: every finite $S$ is contained in such an $R$, with $U$ containing any prescribed $T_0$.

source.place: Finite separable spreading in existing node lem-weil-pbc-spread-finite-separable-extension; Tags 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), 00UC (lemma-standard-etale), 00U2 (lemma-etale); explicit numerator/denominator calculation.

proof.text: Let $D$ be the set of pairs $(T,R)$ where $T\subseteq B$ is finite, $R\subseteq k$ is a subring containing $A_T$, and $\operatorname{Spec}R\to\operatorname{Spec}A_T$ is etale. Order it by $(T,R)\leq(U,R')$ if $T\subseteq U$ and $R\subseteq R'$. This is a partial order: reflexivity and transitivity are those of inclusion; mutual inequalities force equality of both components. It is small because it is a subset of the product of the finite subsets of $B$ with the set of subrings of $k$. It is nonempty by Step 3 with $S=T_0=\varnothing$. Each $A_T\to R$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres] and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine]. Compose it with the smooth polynomial map $\mathbf Q\to A_T$ of [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth], using [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition]. Thus $R$ is smooth over $\mathbf Q$, and in particular finitely presented and of finite type by [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].

source.place: Tags 02GK (lemma-etale-smooth-unramified), 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize); algebra.tex Tags 00T6, 00T7, 00TD; definition of smooth ring map 00T2.

proof.text: Fix $(T,R)\in D$ and a finite $U\supseteq T$ in $B$. The prime $0\subset R$ contracts to $0\subset A_T$ since both are subrings of $k$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-residue-field-separable] at this prime: $E=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ is finite separable, in particular algebraic, over $F_T$. The elements of $U\setminus T$ are algebraically independent over $F_T$: a polynomial relation with rational-function coefficients in $T$ becomes a nonzero polynomial relation among the distinct elements of $U$ after multiplying by a common nonzero denominator in $A_T$, contrary to independence of $B$. By [lem-zl-independence-algebraic-base] they remain independent over $E$, hence over its subring $R$. Consequently the subring $R[U\setminus T]\subseteq k$ is the polynomial ring over $R$ on these variables. It is also the base change $A_U\otimes_{A_T}R$: the homomorphism sends $p\otimes r$ to $pr$; the inverse writes a polynomial uniquely as a sum of monomials in $U\setminus T$ with coefficients in $R$, sending each term $rM$ to $M\otimes r$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change] makes this subring etale over $A_U$.

source.place: Tags 00U3 (lemma-etale-over-field) and 00U2 (lemma-etale), base change; Mathlib Algebra.IsAlgebraic.algebraicIndependent_iff, AlgebraicIndependent/AlgebraicClosure.lean:96; polynomial and tensor identifications written explicitly.

proof.text: For $(T,R)\leq(U,R')$, the intermediate ring $P=R[U\setminus T]$ of Step 5 lies in $R'$, since $R'\supseteq R$ and $R'\supseteq A_U$. Both $P$ and $R'$ are etale over $A_U$. The map $\operatorname{Spec}R'\to\operatorname{Spec}P$ commutes with their maps to $\operatorname{Spec}A_U$, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](3) makes it etale. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres] and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], $P\to R'$ is smooth. The map $R\to P$ is a finite polynomial extension by Step 5, hence smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth]. Composition [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition] proves that the transition inclusion $R\to R'$ is smooth. This argument applies to our componentwise order on pairs, and makes no assertion about arbitrary inclusions between smooth rational subalgebras.

source.place: Tag 02GW (lemma-etale-permanence), followed by etale-to-smooth and algebra.tex Tag 00TD (lemma-compose-smooth).

proof.text: For $(T,R),(T',R')\in D$, choose finite lists of $\mathbf Q$-algebra generators of $R$ and $R'$, which exist by Step 4. Apply Step 3 to the union $S$ of these lists and to $T_0=T\cup T'$. It gives $(U,R'')\in D$ with $U\supseteq T\cup T'$ and $S\subseteq R''$. Since $R''$ contains $\mathbf Q$ and both generating lists, it contains both $R$ and $R'$. Thus $(U,R'')$ is an upper bound in the specified order. Together with nonemptiness this proves directedness. Apply Step 3 also to $S=\{x\}$ for each $x\in k$ to obtain $\bigcup_{(T,R)\in D}R=k$.

source.place: Elementary assembly of Steps 3 and 4: finite generating lists, common upper bound, and singleton coverage.

proof.text: The inclusions form a ring cocone with vertex $k$. Given compatible ring homomorphisms $h_i:R_i\to H$, define $h:k\to H$ by $h(x)=h_i(x)$ at any stage containing $x$. If two stages contain $x$, a common upper bound and compatibility give the same value, so $h$ is well defined. For $x,y\in k$, put their stages in a common upper stage; the ring-map identities there give $h(x+y)=h(x)+h(y)$, $h(xy)=h(x)h(y)$, and preservation of $0,1$. Its restrictions are the $h_i$, and coverage makes it unique. This is precisely the ring colimit universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For any fixed index $i$, the tail $\{j\mid i\leq j\}$ still covers $k$: put $i$ and a stage containing $x$ into a common upper bound. The same argument gives $k$ as the colimit of this tail in commutative $R_i$-algebras, since the unique assembled ring map respects the specified map out of $R_i$.

source.place: Elementary cocone universal-property argument, also for each tail; BMT Theorem 7.5(1), field case, written as a union of coefficient rings.

proof.text: Fix $i$ and write $R=R_i\subseteq k$, a domain with fraction field $E=\operatorname{Frac}(R)\subseteq k$. Flatness: the only prime of $k$ is $0$, its contraction to $R$ is $0$, and the induced localization map is $R_{(0)}=E\to k_{(0)}=k$. It is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat], since $k$ is an $E$-vector space, so $R\to k$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-map-local-criterion]. Fibres: let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be prime. If $\mathfrak p\ne0$, choose $0\ne a\in\mathfrak p$. In $k\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ one has $1\otimes1=a^{-1}a\otimes1=a^{-1}\otimes\bar a=0$, so this fibre is the zero ring. If $\mathfrak p=0$, then $\kappa(0)=E$ and the fibre is $k$: the map $x\otimes(r/s)\mapsto xr/s$ has inverse $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, and the second composite is the identity because every nonzero $s\in R$ is already invertible in $k$. Both fibres are Noetherian: the zero ring has one ideal, and a field has only $0$ and the unit ideal. Geometric regularity: $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ has characteristic $0$, so by [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] its only finite purely inseparable extension is $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ itself. It remains to show that each fibre is a regular ring. The zero ring is Noetherian and has no prime ideals, so it is vacuously regular. The field $k$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-field-regular-ring]. Hence $R_i\to k$ is regular in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], for every $i$, and all clauses are proved.
